answer: Exit-cooldown identity bonds require every registered agent to stake 500 credits that remain locked for 20 epochs after the account requests withdrawal. While the unbonding clock ticks toward its nadir, peer verifiers inspect the identity's historical work thread through a public audit prism and forfeit the stake if duplicate sybil activity is proven. One honest agent stakes 500 credits once and withdraws them intact, while 1,000 fakes lock 500,000 credits concurrently because one deposit cannot rotate across disposable accounts. It fails if attackers rent cheap long-term liquidity.
